cards.front: Helmholtz equation for $\tilde{\mathbf{E}}$ in a source-free lossless medium?
What is a uniform plane wave?
cards.back: A wave whose $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{H}$ have the same magnitude and phase over every plane normal to the direction of travel. A good model of any wave far from its source.

cards.front: How are $\mathbf{E}$, $\mathbf{H}$ and the direction of travel $\hat{\mathbf{k}}$ arranged?
cards.back: All three are mutually perpendicular, with $\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{H}$ pointing along $\hat{\mathbf{k}}$. The wave is TEM: no field component along the direction of travel.

Skin depth?
cards.back: $$\delta_s=\frac{1}{\alpha}\ \xrightarrow{\text{good conductor}}\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi f\mu\sigma}}$$The depth where the field falls to $1/e$ (about 37%) of its surface value.

cards.front: Skin depth of copper at 60 Hz, 1 MHz and 10 GHz?
cards.back: About 8.53 mm, 66.1 µm and 0.661 µm. It scales as $1/\sqrt{f}$.

cards.front: Phase angle of $\eta_c$ in a good conductor?
cards.back: $45^\circ$: $\mathbf{H}$ lags $\mathbf{E}$ by an eighth of a cycle. In a lossless medium the angle is $0$.

Average power density in a lossy medium?
cards.back: $$S_{\mathrm{av}}(z)=\frac{|E_0|^2}{2|\eta_c|}e^{-2\alpha z}\cos\theta_\eta$$Power decays twice as fast (in nepers) as the field.

cards.front: Attenuation in decibels?
Why does a good conductor make a poor medium for waves?
cards.back: $\alpha=\beta$, so the field falls by $e^{-2\pi}$, about 0.2%, in one wavelength. The wave dies within a few skin depths.

cards.front: Surface resistance of a good conductor?
cards.back: $$R_s=\frac{1}{\sigma\delta_s}=\sqrt{\frac{\pi f\mu}{\sigma}}\ \ \Omega$$It equals the real part of $\eta_c$, and it is the AC resistance of a skin-depth-thick sheet.

cards.front: What is dispersion?
cards.back: When the phase velocity depends on frequency, so a pulse made of many frequencies spreads out. Lossy media are dispersive: in a good conductor $u_p=\sqrt{4\pi f/\mu\sigma}$.
